figures.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific infographic.
Edit the supplied infographic for a scientific paper, retaining the light white background, navy typography, teal and amber palette, clean diagrams, 16:9 landscape aspect, and excellent legibility. Save as a new image, not a replacement. Produce a high resolution landscape image.
Primary change: put the operational questions FIRST. Remove the two theoretical boxes from above the columns. Make the four operational columns the main upper/middle content, then place a smaller separate interpretive strip at the very bottom, BELOW the scientific message, without any arrows from that strip into the operational diagrams.
Title exact: "Four questions about form"
Four columns, retain the existing visual concepts and use these exact labels:
"POSSIBILITY" / "What do the rules permit?" / "Rules"
"ACCESSIBILITY" / "What can be reached?" / "Body + history + resources"
"RECOGNITION" / "What counts as the same form?" / "Observer + scale"
"CONTINUATION" / "What keeps it available?" / "Body + record + reader"
For recognition retain coarse/fine grid and eye, labels "Coarse" and "Fine". For continuation retain body/record loop with arrows labeled "write" and "read"; body and record labeled. For accessibility retain schematic two-well landscape, not measured data.
Below the columns use this exact main message: "Embodiment makes possibilities accessible and maintainable."
Smaller line: "Schematic framework, not a measured map of all forms."
Then separated by a thin gray rule, small heading "OPTIONAL INTERPRETIVE CONTEXT"
Two small side-by-side boxes: "Wolfram: ruliad" / "Proposed account of computational possibility"; "Levin: Platonic space" / "Proposed independently real patterns".
Footer inside that bottom strip: "Neither ontology is tested by these simulations."
No chronological arrows between the four columns. Do not introduce any new quantitative claim. Clearly separate the bottom theoretical context from the operational diagrams.

Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one finished scientific infographic for a research preprint, landscape 16:9, high resolution, ideally 3840 x 2160. It will also be used as a standalone slide. Original new image; no reference image. Style: clean editorial scientific illustration with precise, flat vector-like linework, ample whitespace, warm white background (#FBFCFA), deep navy text (#12333E), teal (#087F8C), restrained amber (#D99A25), pale teal and pale amber fills. No gradients, textures, dark panels, decoration, watermark, or invented plots. Large readable sans-serif typography; match a coherent three-figure series.

Title: 'Three tests of pattern continuity'. Subtitle: 'Selected simulation results; different mechanisms'. Three horizontal panels separated by thin light-grey vertical rules. Give the first panel slightly more width, and keep every label large enough to read when printed across a journal page.

Left panel heading: 'A  REHOMING'. Secondary label: 'Strict-eight'. Diagram: a grey old-anchor disc at left labeled 'Old anchor', then a small amber break slash on a dashed trajectory, followed by an ellipsis representing a strictly later time, then exactly EIGHT teal daughter discs in one single horizontal followed-lineage chain. Number these eight discs 1 through 8. Keep all eight inside a single pale teal coherence enclosure; a bracket beneath all eight denotes the whole window. A light mesh beneath the row can suggest comparisons among all daughter pairs without obscuring the sequence. Do not draw a branching family or a binary tree. Visible lines below: '8 inherited daughters' and 'All 28 pairs coherent' and 'Each distinct from the old anchor'. Small status line: 'A finite lineage event'. No similarity thresholds or quantitative axes inside the artwork.

Middle panel heading: 'B  REPAIR'. Diagram: a small tissue grid labeled 'Body' and a partially damaged record-card labeled 'Record'. Show a two-way feedback loop: record-to-body arrow 'read', body-to-record arrow 'write'. From the resulting record, a separate arrow leads to a fresh tissue grid labeled 'Fresh-body assay'. Use one amber disruption mark to show damage, but keep some original record content and body structure visible. Visible explanation: 'Surviving body structure improves record repair'. Small status line: 'One repair episode'. Do not imply that the body is the sole information source, and do not draw an infinite repair loop or show invented before/after scores.

Right panel heading: 'C  RENEWAL'. Diagram: a small encoded record leads into a fresh cellular-automaton grid; its resulting activity writes a new record; a dashed vertical boundary separates this from the next fresh grid. Diagram labels only: 'Record', 'Fresh body', 'Rewrite', 'Next body'. The old body does not cross the replacement boundary. Visible result lines: 'CA: 64-bit payload, 16 generations' and 'Shared reading and writing machinery'. Beneath, a small amber contrast strip: 'L17 tissue loop: information declines'. Small status line: 'Renewal depends on architecture'. Do not depict 64 bits as an autonomous organism, and do not draw comparative bar charts or synthetic trajectories.

Bottom takeaway in large navy text: 'Coherence, repair and renewal are different claims.' Small secondary line: 'Schematic mechanisms; see captions for protocols and controls.' Use only the quoted visible text, with generous margins. This is a scientifically bounded explanatory diagram, not raw experimental data.

Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific infographic.
Edit the supplied scientific infographic, preserving its polished light-background 16:9 landscape style, navy text, teal and amber palette, rounded three-column panels, and clear biological illustrations. Produce a high resolution landscape image. Correct the central evidence panel to reflect a completed editable regulatory-state lineage, not the older 12-replacement result. This is a conceptual model summary, never a medical efficacy image.
Title exact: "From cell state to collective capacity"
Subtitle exact: "Biological connections and the next scientific question"
Left panel: heading "BIOLOGICAL PRECEDENT"; subheading "Cell state". Retain simple cell with exposure, retained state and later response, labeled exactly "Exposure", "Retained state", "Later response". Bottom text "History can change a cell's later response."
Middle panel: heading "DEMONSTRATED IN A MODEL"; subheading "Editable state lineage". Replace the old donor-recipient scene and the old '12 carrier replacements' claim with a spacious vertical four-step sequence. Use small groups of exactly three cells to illustrate each stage. Exact stage labels, large and readable:
"Write M"
"3 complete replacements"
"Rewrite current carriers to E"
"3 further replacements"
Use teal for M group and amber for E group, clear small downward arrows linking the four steps, no branching implication and no cell-division icon. Tiny relevant secondary label after replacements: "Old carriers removed".
Below sequence: "Acquired state is transmitted, revised, and transmitted again."
Small condition line: "Cells, cues, contacts, and schedules supplied"
Right panel: heading "OPEN HYPOTHESIS"; subheading "Collective capacity". Retain different cells rearranging around a disruption, with labels "Disruption", "New roles", "Same function". Bottom: "Can a group preserve function by changing roles?" and "Can new members inherit that capacity?"
Main bottom message exact: "Editable state continuity is demonstrated; inherited flexible competence remains open."
Smaller footer: "Model E/M states are not health or cancer diagnoses. Biological parallels motivate tests."
Keep all text inside generous margins, render exact spelling, do not include '12', success percentages, clinical promises, or claims of autonomous reproduction.
figures.correction: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied scientific infographic. Keep ALL typography, text, layout, background, left panel, right panel, and footer unchanged. Change ONLY the colors of two rows of three cells in the CENTER panel to correctly encode states. Center row 1 'Write M' remains teal (M). Center row 2 '3 complete replacements' must also be TEAL (M), exactly the same teal as row 1: transmission preserves M. Center row 3 'Rewrite current carriers to E' must be AMBER (E), exactly the same amber as row 4: rewrite changes M to E. Center row 4 '3 further replacements' remains AMBER (E). Thus from top to bottom the center panel colors MUST be TEAL, TEAL, AMBER, AMBER. Recolor both nuclei and cell outlines/fills consistently for each changed row. This is a scientific correction, not aesthetic alternation. Do not alternate teal/amber/teal/amber. Do not modify any text, arrows, or other image element. Preserve original 16:9 aspect ratio and high resolution.
